meta.blurb: Cyrano can fight a duel and make up a poem at the same time, but he is sure no woman could love his nose. His cousin Roxane loves a handsome soldier with no words. Cyrano has plenty, and he lends them.
meta.bible: Cyrano de Bergerac: a Gascon soldier, poet and swordsman with a huge nose; proud, brave, witty, generous; secretly loves his cousin Roxane. Roxane: Cyrano's beautiful, clever cousin, who loves poetry and fine words. Christian de Neuvillette: a handsome young soldier who is a poor speaker and loves Roxane; he joins the Cadets of Gascony. Comte de Guiche: a powerful nobleman who loves Roxane; he later becomes a duke and admires Cyrano. Vicomte de Valvert: a foolish nobleman who insults Cyrano's nose. Montfleury: a fat actor whom Cyrano drives off the stage. Le Bret: Cyrano's loyal friend. Ragueneau: a pastry cook who loves poetry and lets poets pay in verses. Ligniere: a poet and drunkard, Cyrano's friend. Cadets of Gascony: the company of soldiers in which Cyrano and Christian serve. Hôtel de Bourgogne: the Paris theatre in 1640. Porte de Nesle: the gate where Cyrano fights a hundred men. Arras: the besieged town where the Cadets are sent to war. Paris, France, Gascony, Spanish, Spain. Capuchin: the monk who marries Roxane and Christian. Panache: Cyrano's gallant spirit, symbolised by a white plume. Carbon de Castel-Jaloux: the captain of the Cadets. Bellerose: the manager of the theatre. Lise: Ragueneau's wife. Cuigy and Brissaille: friends in the crowd. Cardinal Richelieu: the most powerful man in France. Agrippine: Cyrano's tragedy. Bergerac: the country place where Cyrano and Roxane played as children. Sister Marthe and Sister Claire: nuns in the convent garden. Duenna: Roxane's old servant. Molière: the playwright. Saturday: the day Cyrano visits. Falsehood, Compromise, Prejudice, Cowardice, Folly: the enemies Cyrano fights in the air. Voice and tone: witty, passionate and heroic, bitter-sweet; set in France in 1640 and fifteen years later in 1655; fights are shown with no gore; Christian dies in battle, and Cyrano dies after a log is dropped on his head by an enemy.
chapters: The Man Who Stopped the Play
The Secret She Came to Tell

beats.scene: A noisy crowd of nobles, soldiers and pages fills a grand Paris theatre
beats.summary: In 1640 a noisy crowd fills the Hôtel de Bourgogne theatre in Paris, waiting for a play.

beats.scene: Pickpockets slip between gentlemen who guard their purses in the candlelit hall
beats.summary: Pickpockets work the crowd, pages play tricks, and gentlemen keep a hand on their purses while the audience waits.

beats.scene: Christian looks anxiously at an empty box above the crowded theatre
beats.summary: Christian de Neuvillette, a handsome new soldier, loves a lady he has never spoken to and watches for her.

beats.scene: Ligniere raises his cup and speaks into Christian's ear
beats.summary: Christian asks the poet Ligniere, who knows everyone in Paris, and Ligniere tells him the lady's name is Roxane.

beats.scene: Ligniere nods toward a grand nobleman and a pale young man
beats.summary: Ligniere warns that the powerful Comte de Guiche wants Roxane too and means to give her to a weak nobleman.

beats.scene: Christian looks down at his plain soldier's coat and shakes his head
beats.summary: Christian admits that he is no poet: in front of a clever woman his tongue turns to stone.

beats.scene: The crowd talks excitedly about a swordsman who has banned an actor
beats.summary: The crowd gossips about Cyrano, the Gascon poet and swordsman with an enormous nose, who has forbidden Montfleury to act for a month.

beats.scene: Roxane enters her box with her old servant and Christian stares up speechless
beats.summary: Roxane takes her seat in the box, and Christian can hardly breathe.

beats.scene: The Comte de Guiche and the Vicomte de Valvert take chairs on the stage
beats.summary: The Comte de Guiche and the Vicomte de Valvert settle on the stage, and at last the play begins with Montfleury's entrance.

beats.scene: A voice thunders from the crowd and the whole theatre turns around
beats.summary: Montfleury has hardly begun when a great voice from the crowd shouts that it forbade him to appear for a month.

beats.scene: Cyrano stands on a chair, arms folded, hat tilted, nose enormous
beats.summary: Cyrano stands on a chair with his arms folded, his hat on one side and a huge nose, and the crowd stares.

beats.scene: Cyrano calmly counts to three and tells the actor to leave
beats.summary: Cyrano tells Montfleury that he will count to three, and at three the actor's round face must vanish like a moon in an eclipse.

beats.scene: The crowd splits into shouting groups while Montfleury hesitates on the stage
beats.summary: Some of the crowd cheer Cyrano and others shout for the play to go on, while poor Montfleury cannot decide what to do.

beats.scene: Cyrano dares anyone to step forward and nobody does
beats.summary: Cyrano declares that he will cut off the ears of anyone who objects, and no one dares to step forward.

beats.scene: Cyrano throws a heavy purse of gold to the theatre manager
beats.summary: Cyrano pays Bellerose, the theatre manager, with a purse of gold for the ruined play, and the crowd laughs and cheers.

beats.scene: A marquis asks Cyrano why he hates the actor so much
beats.summary: A marquis asks why Cyrano hates Montfleury, and Cyrano gives two reasons: the actor is terrible, and the second one he keeps to himself.

beats.scene: The Vicomte de Valvert steps forward with a sneer and mentions the nose
beats.summary: The Vicomte de Valvert steps forward and sneers that Cyrano has a very large nose, and Cyrano agrees that it is.

beats.scene: Cyrano lists the many witty insults the Vicomte should have said instead
beats.summary: Cyrano tells the Vicomte he could have said much better things about the nose, and he begins to show him with a fierce one.

beats.scene: Cyrano gives friendly, curious and gentle jokes about his own nose
beats.summary: Cyrano goes on with friendly, curious and gentle ways of joking about his nose, each wittier than the last.

beats.scene: Cyrano says the Vicomte has no wit and will have to fight a poet
beats.summary: Cyrano tells the Vicomte that he has no wit and no manners, and says he will fight him and make a poem at the same time.

beats.scene: Cyrano throws off his cloak while the crowd makes a ring of space
beats.summary: The crowd clears a ring, Cyrano throws off his cloak, and he names his ballad the duel at the Hôtel de Bourgogne.

beats.scene: Cyrano begins his poem as the swords touch
beats.summary: As the swords touch, Cyrano begins his poem, speaking each line in time with his blade.

beats.scene: The Vicomte attacks again and again but cannot touch Cyrano
beats.summary: The Vicomte lunges again and again, but Cyrano turns every stroke aside without losing a single rhyme.

beats.scene: Roxane leans from her box with bright eyes while Christian and the Comte watch
beats.summary: Roxane leans from her box with shining eyes, Christian watches her watching, and the Comte de Guiche frowns.

beats.scene: Cyrano tells the Vicomte exactly when he will be hit
beats.summary: Cyrano tells the sweating Vicomte that at the last line of the poem, the point of his sword will touch him.

beats.scene: At the last line Cyrano's sword strikes and the Vicomte falls
beats.summary: At the very last line of the poem, Cyrano's sword strikes and the Vicomte staggers and falls, wounded but alive.

beats.scene: Cyrano bows to the cheering crowd as the Comte leaves in anger
beats.summary: The crowd cheers Cyrano's name, Cyrano bows, and the Comte de Guiche leaves in anger with the wounded Vicomte.

beats.scene: The empty theatre grows quiet as Le Bret scolds Cyrano
beats.summary: When the theatre is nearly empty, Le Bret praises his friend but scolds him for making powerful enemies.

beats.scene: Cyrano says he would rather be free and fight alone
beats.summary: Cyrano answers that he would rather be free and fight alone than be rich, safe and the pet of a great man.

beats.scene: Cyrano finally confesses that he loves his cousin Roxane
beats.summary: Pressed by Le Bret for the second reason, Cyrano admits at last that he loves his beautiful cousin Roxane.

beats.scene: Cyrano touches his nose and speaks sadly to Le Bret in the empty theatre
beats.summary: Cyrano tells Le Bret that no woman could love a man with his nose, and he can only joke bitterly about it.

beats.scene: Le Bret reminds Cyrano that Roxane watched the duel with shining eyes
beats.summary: Le Bret reminds Cyrano that Roxane watched the duel with shining eyes, but Cyrano says she would smile at any brave man.

beats.scene: An old servant woman appears at the door of the empty theatre
beats.summary: The Duenna, Roxane's old servant, appears at the door and asks to speak to Cyrano.

beats.scene: The Duenna gives Cyrano a message from Roxane
beats.summary: The Duenna says that Roxane wants to meet Cyrano the next day, alone, and Cyrano names the pastry shop of Ragueneau as the place.

beats.scene: Cyrano leaps with joy and promises to fight the whole world
beats.summary: Cyrano is wild with joy and cries that after such news he could fight an army, whether of giants or of a hundred men.

beats.scene: Ligniere rushes in, pale and shaking, and begs for help
beats.summary: Ligniere rushes in pale and trembling: he wrote a song against a great lord, and a hundred men are waiting to attack him at the Porte de Nesle.

beats.scene: Cyrano promises to see Ligniere home himself
beats.summary: Cyrano laughs and says he will escort Ligniere home himself, and that all hundred men will be sorry.

beats.scene: Cyrano calls the crowd to bring torches to watch
beats.summary: Word spreads, and Cyrano invites actors, musicians, soldiers and citizens to follow him with torches and watch the fight.

beats.scene: A torchlit procession winds through the night streets toward the gate
beats.summary: The torchlit procession winds through the dark streets, and the moon rises over the roofs of Paris as they near the gate.

beats.scene: Cyrano faces a hundred swordsmen at the gate and wins by moonlight
beats.summary: At the Porte de Nesle Cyrano stands alone against a hundred men, and by the end of the night the street is empty.

beats.scene: Dawn light falls on the busy ovens and spits of Ragueneau's shop
beats.summary: At dawn in Ragueneau's pastry shop, the ovens are hot, the spits are turning, and the cook-poet is already at work.

beats.scene: Apprentices wrap pastries in pages of poems
beats.summary: Ragueneau's apprentices wrap the pastries in sheets of poetry, because the poets who pay him with verses leave them everywhere.

beats.scene: Ragueneau sings a recipe in rhyme while his helpers laugh
beats.summary: Ragueneau proudly recites a recipe for almond tarts in the form of a poem, while his helpers laugh and listen.

beats.scene: Cyrano arrives tired at the shop door and Ragueneau greets him in awe
beats.summary: Cyrano arrives at the shop tired but cheerful, and Ragueneau greets him in awe, since all Paris is talking of the battle at the gate.

beats.scene: Cyrano asks Ragueneau to clear the shop when the lady arrives
beats.summary: Cyrano asks Ragueneau to keep the shop empty and quiet at the hour when a lady is due to arrive, and Ragueneau understands.

beats.scene: Cyrano writes a love letter at a table and fights his own courage
beats.summary: Alone at a table, Cyrano writes a love letter to Roxane and then wonders whether he will ever have the courage to give it to her.

beats.scene: The Duenna arrives to say that Roxane is coming and receives cakes
beats.summary: The Duenna arrives to say that Roxane is on her way, and Cyrano cleverly gives her a plate of cakes so that she will keep busy.

beats.scene: Roxane enters the shop and takes Cyrano's hands with a warm smile
beats.summary: Roxane arrives like a ray of sunshine, takes Cyrano's hands and calls him her dear cousin.

beats.scene: Roxane and Cyrano remember their games as children in the country
beats.summary: Roxane reminds Cyrano of the days at Bergerac when he played the brave knight and she was his friend, and he climbed the trees for her.

beats.scene: Roxane thanks Cyrano for the duel and says she is glad about the Vicomte
beats.summary: Roxane thanks Cyrano for beating the Vicomte, because the Comte de Guiche wanted her to marry that foolish man.

beats.scene: Roxane holds Cyrano's hands and tells him she has a secret
beats.summary: Roxane tells Cyrano that she has a secret and needs his help, and Cyrano hopes for a moment that it is love for him.

beats.scene: Roxane says she loves a man and Cyrano turns pale
beats.summary: Roxane tells Cyrano that she is in love, and Cyrano turns pale and waits to hear the name.

beats.scene: Roxane describes a handsome Cadet she has never spoken to
beats.summary: Roxane says she loves a handsome young man in the Cadets of Gascony, in Cyrano's own company, and that they have never spoken.

beats.scene: Cyrano asks questions and hides his pain behind a joke
beats.summary: Cyrano asks whether the young man is brave and clever, and he hides his pain behind jokes.

beats.scene: Roxane asks Cyrano to protect the Cadet from the other Gascons
beats.summary: Roxane fears that the proud Gascons will pick quarrels with a newcomer, and she asks Cyrano to protect him.

beats.scene: Cyrano promises to protect his rival and make him write to Roxane
beats.summary: Cyrano promises to protect the young man, and Roxane also asks him to make the Cadet write her a letter.

beats.scene: Roxane leaves, and the Duenna comes out of the next room with her cakes
beats.summary: Roxane leaves with a kiss of thanks, and the Duenna hurries out of the next room with her arms full of cakes.

beats.scene: Cyrano alone in the shop speaks bitterly to himself
beats.summary: Alone in the shop, Cyrano laughs bitterly at himself for becoming the guard of his own rival.

beats.scene: Cadets of Gascony crowd noisily into the shop with Captain Carbon
beats.summary: The Cadets of Gascony crowd noisily into the shop with their captain, Carbon de Castel-Jaloux, to cheer Cyrano for the fight at the gate.

beats.scene: The Cadets cheer, hungry and poor but proud
beats.summary: The Cadets are hungry and poor but proud, and they hail Cyrano and call for food and songs.

beats.scene: Cyrano smiles modestly while the Cadets beg for the story of the gate
beats.summary: The Cadets beg Cyrano to tell the story of the gate, and he gives a short, modest answer: it was nothing much.

beats.scene: The Comte de Guiche enters and the cheerful Cadets fall silent
beats.summary: The Comte de Guiche enters the shop, the Cadets fall silent, and Cyrano keeps his hat on his head.

beats.scene: The Comte offers to present Cyrano's play to Cardinal Richelieu
beats.summary: The Comte offers to show Cyrano's tragedy, Agrippine, to the great Cardinal Richelieu, who might make him famous.

beats.scene: The Comte adds that the Cardinal will want one line changed
beats.summary: The Comte adds that the Cardinal would only ask for a few lines to be changed, and Cyrano grows still.

beats.scene: Cyrano refuses to change a single word of his play
beats.summary: Cyrano thanks the Comte politely and refuses: he will not change a single comma, not for a cardinal and not for a king.

beats.scene: Le Bret despairs while the Cadets cheer the refusal
beats.summary: Le Bret groans that Cyrano has thrown away a fortune, but the Cadets cheer, and Cyrano says that he would rather be nobody.

beats.scene: The Comte leaves in a cold rage and Cyrano makes a joke
beats.summary: The Comte leaves in a cold rage and warns that Cyrano's pride will ruin him, and Cyrano answers with a joke.

beats.scene: A young Cadet named Christian is introduced to the company
beats.summary: Carbon introduces a new Cadet, Christian de Neuvillette, and the other Cadets whisper that nobody must mention Cyrano's nose.

beats.scene: Christian makes a clumsy joke about the nose to show he is not afraid
beats.summary: Christian, determined to prove himself, makes a clumsy joke about Cyrano's nose, and the shop falls dead silent.

beats.scene: Cyrano controls his anger because Christian is Roxane's love
beats.summary: Cyrano turns white and grips the back of a chair, but he controls his anger because he remembers who this young man is.

beats.scene: Cyrano embraces Christian and tells him a secret in a quiet corner
beats.summary: Cyrano calls Christian over, shakes his hand, and tells him in a corner that he is Roxane's cousin.

beats.scene: Christian learns that Roxane loves him and is wild with joy
beats.summary: Cyrano tells Christian that Roxane loves him, and Christian is wild with joy.

beats.scene: Christian admits he is a poor speaker and fears he will fail
beats.summary: Christian suddenly turns gloomy: he is a poor speaker, and Roxane will soon be bored by a man with no words.

beats.scene: Cyrano offers to lend Christian his wit
beats.summary: Cyrano offers a bargain: he will lend Christian his words, and Christian will lend him his handsome face.

beats.scene: Christian accepts and Cyrano hands him a letter
beats.summary: Christian accepts with wonder, and Cyrano gives him the letter he wrote that morning, to be learned by heart and sent as his own.

beats.scene: Cyrano writes by candlelight while Christian sleeps
beats.summary: Over the following days, Cyrano writes letter after letter in Christian's name late into the night.

beats.scene: Roxane reads the letters by lamplight and falls more in love
beats.summary: Roxane reads each letter by lamplight, sighs with pleasure and falls more in love with Christian with every page.

beats.scene: A tear falls on a page as Cyrano writes
beats.summary: As Cyrano writes, a tear falls on the page, and he realises that he is writing his own feelings in Christian's name.

beats.scene: Ragueneau weeps in his ruined shop while a musketeer leaves with Lise
beats.summary: Ragueneau is ruined: the poets have eaten everything, his wife Lise has run away with a musketeer, and he wants to hang himself.

beats.scene: Cyrano finds Ragueneau a place in Roxane's house
beats.summary: Cyrano scolds Ragueneau for his foolishness and finds him a place as a servant in Roxane's house.

beats.scene: Evening falls on a quiet house with a balcony covered in jasmine
beats.summary: Several weeks later, evening falls on Roxane's quiet house, with its balcony hung with jasmine and its garden wall.

beats.scene: Ragueneau now works as Roxane's servant and writes poems on shopping lists
beats.summary: Ragueneau, now Roxane's servant, scribbles verses on shopping lists while the Duenna scolds him for forgetting the bread.

beats.scene: Roxane tells her old servant that she is waiting for Christian tonight
beats.summary: Roxane tells the Duenna that Christian is coming tonight, and that she can hardly wait to hear his voice.

beats.scene: Roxane reads a letter aloud and the Duenna shrugs
beats.summary: Roxane reads part of a letter aloud and sighs with joy, but the Duenna says that men are usually more handsome than clever.

beats.scene: A servant announces the Comte de Guiche and Roxane hides the letters
beats.summary: A servant announces the Comte de Guiche at the door, and Roxane hides her letters and prepares to be polite.

beats.scene: The Comte, in soldier's armour, says goodbye because he is leaving for the war
beats.summary: The Comte de Guiche arrives in armour and tells Roxane that he leaves for the war tonight, and he asks her not to forget him.

beats.scene: The Comte reveals that the Cadets of Gascony will march with him
beats.summary: The Comte mentions that Cyrano's company, the Cadets of Gascony, will march to Arras as well, and Roxane grows pale.

beats.scene: Roxane cleverly suggests that the Comte leave the Cadets behind
beats.summary: Roxane asks how the Comte can best punish Cyrano, and then suggests that he leave the Cadets behind in Paris while others fight.

beats.scene: The Comte loves the idea and promises to give the order at once
beats.summary: The Comte loves the idea, thinks Roxane is taking his side at last, and promises to give the order at once.

beats.scene: The Comte promises to send word later and leaves, and Roxane rushes to prepare
beats.summary: Before he goes, the Comte says he will send a messenger tonight with a letter, and Roxane quickly rushes to the garden to wait for Christian.

beats.scene: Christian and Cyrano arrive below the balcony; Christian says he will speak himself
beats.summary: Christian arrives in the dark street with Cyrano, and says that tonight he will speak for himself, without any help.

beats.scene: Roxane appears on the balcony and Christian can only say he loves her
beats.summary: Roxane appears on the balcony, and Christian can only say again and again that he loves her.

beats.scene: Roxane is disappointed and goes inside, leaving Christian alone
beats.summary: Roxane is disappointed that he has no more to say, and she goes back inside, leaving Christian alone.

beats.scene: Christian calls desperately for Cyrano to come out of the shadows
beats.summary: Christian calls desperately for Cyrano, who steps out of the shadows and says that he had expected this.

beats.scene: Cyrano hides below the balcony and Roxane returns when Christian calls
beats.summary: Cyrano hides in the black shadow under the balcony, and Roxane comes back out when Christian calls her name.

beats.scene: Cyrano whispers words that Christian repeats badly
beats.summary: Cyrano whispers fine words, and Christian repeats them slowly and badly, so that Roxane begins to suspect a trick.

beats.scene: Cyrano pushes Christian aside and speaks himself in the dark
beats.summary: Cyrano pushes Christian aside and speaks in his own voice from the dark, lower and warmer than before.

beats.scene: Cyrano speaks of the stars and Roxane is enchanted
beats.summary: Cyrano speaks of the stars, the flowers and the night, and Roxane, enchanted, says that her heart is flying.

beats.scene: Cyrano explains what a kiss is and Roxane begs for it
beats.summary: Roxane says she wants a kiss, and Cyrano answers with a beautiful speech about what a kiss really is.

beats.scene: Christian climbs to the balcony while Cyrano watches from the darkness
beats.summary: Cyrano sends Christian up to the balcony to receive the kiss, and he watches in silence from the shadows below.

beats.scene: The Duenna hurries into the garden to announce a monk at the door
beats.summary: The Duenna hurries into the garden to say that a Capuchin monk is at the door with a letter for Roxane.

beats.scene: The Capuchin peers at the house numbers and hands Roxane a letter
beats.summary: The old Capuchin peers at the doors, looking for a lady called Roxane, and gives her the Comte de Guiche's letter.

beats.scene: Roxane reads a false version of the letter aloud to the monk
beats.summary: Roxane reads the letter aloud, but she invents the end, so that it seems to say that the Comte wants the monk to marry her to Christian at once.

beats.scene: The honest old monk is touched and agrees to hurry
beats.summary: The honest old monk is touched by the Comte's kindness, and he agrees to perform the wedding at once.

beats.scene: Roxane leads the monk, the Duenna and Christian inside
beats.summary: Roxane leads the monk, the Duenna and Christian into the house and tells Cyrano to keep watch outside.

beats.scene: Cyrano alone in the dark, thinking of the wedding
beats.summary: Alone in the street, Cyrano thinks bitterly that the woman he loves is being married to the man who borrowed his words.

beats.scene: A masked man in a cloak appears, and Cyrano recognises the Comte
beats.summary: A cloaked figure with a mask creeps along the street, and Cyrano recognises the Comte de Guiche, who has come back instead of marching.

beats.scene: Cyrano drops suddenly from above and lands at the Comte's feet
beats.summary: Cyrano climbs up, swings out and lets himself fall with a great thud right at the feet of the astonished Comte.

beats.scene: Cyrano says he has just fallen from the moon
beats.summary: Cyrano rises, looks around in confusion and declares that he has just fallen from the moon.

beats.scene: Cyrano explains how he reached the moon and keeps the Comte talking
beats.summary: Cyrano keeps the Comte talking with a long, absurd story of the ways he travelled to the moon, and the Comte slowly forgets his hurry.

beats.scene: The monk comes out of the house, and Cyrano ends his story
beats.summary: The door opens and the monk comes out: the wedding is done, and Cyrano ends his moon story with a flourish.

beats.scene: Roxane and Christian step out hand in hand, married
beats.summary: Roxane and Christian step out hand in hand, and Roxane calmly tells the Comte that they have just been married.

beats.scene: The Comte realises he has been tricked by all of them
beats.summary: The Comte sees that he has been tricked by Roxane, by Cyrano and by the monk's mistake, and he shakes with anger.

beats.scene: The Comte orders the Cadets to march to the war at Arras
beats.summary: In his rage the Comte changes his order: Cyrano's company will not stay in Paris but will march to the front at Arras tonight.

beats.scene: Roxane begs for mercy but the Comte refuses
beats.summary: Roxane begs the Comte to spare Christian, but the Comte coldly refuses, and Cyrano says that the Cadets will be delighted.

beats.scene: Roxane makes Cyrano promise to guard Christian and make him write
beats.summary: Left alone with Cyrano, Roxane makes him promise that Christian will never be in danger and will write to her every day.

beats.scene: Roxane says a tender farewell to Christian
beats.summary: Roxane and Christian say a tender farewell in the darkness, and Cyrano turns his back and looks at the stars.

beats.scene: Drums beat in the street and the Cadets gather in lines
beats.summary: Drums beat in the street, and the Cadets of Gascony gather in lines with their packs and muskets, ready to march.

beats.scene: Roxane waves a handkerchief from the balcony as the Cadets march away
beats.summary: The Cadets march away singing, and Roxane waves a handkerchief from her balcony until they are out of sight.

beats.scene: Cyrano begins his first letter by a campfire on the road to Arras
beats.summary: On the road north the army makes camp, and Cyrano begins the first of the daily letters by the light of a campfire.

beats.scene: Grey dawn over a muddy camp outside the high walls of Arras
beats.summary: At the siege of Arras, grey dawn rises over a cold, muddy camp of tents and earthworks in front of the walls of the town.

beats.scene: Hungry Cadets lie wrapped in their cloaks, with nothing to eat
beats.summary: The Cadets of Gascony have eaten almost nothing for days, and they lie wrapped in their cloaks, pale and thin.

beats.scene: An old Cadet plays a Gascon tune and the others grow homesick
beats.summary: An old Cadet plays a tune from the hills of Gascony on his pipe, and the others grow homesick and some of them weep.

beats.scene: Cyrano jokes the Cadets out of their sadness
beats.summary: Cyrano strides in and jokes the Cadets out of their sadness, reminding them that they are soldiers and the pride of Gascony.

beats.scene: Cyrano slips out of the camp before dawn in a dark cloak
beats.summary: Before dawn, Cyrano pulls on a dark cloak and quietly slips out of the camp, with a letter hidden in his coat.

beats.scene: Cyrano creeps through the Spanish lines in the mist
beats.summary: Cyrano creeps through the mist and the Spanish lines, crawling past sentries and hiding in ditches, to get his letter to a messenger.

beats.scene: Cyrano returns hurt and Le Bret scolds him
beats.summary: Cyrano returns in the evening with a bullet hole in his hat, and Le Bret scolds him for risking his life for a letter.

beats.scene: Christian asks Cyrano why he goes out every day
beats.summary: Christian asks Cyrano why he goes through the enemy lines each day, and Cyrano answers that it is to post a letter.

beats.scene: Christian asks to hear what Cyrano writes
beats.summary: Christian asks what Cyrano wrote today, and Cyrano recites a few lines so beautiful that the listening Cadets fall silent.

beats.scene: A sentry shouts that a coach is rolling across the fields
beats.summary: At dawn a sentry shouts that a coach is rolling across the fields toward the camp, and the Cadets scramble to their feet in amazement.

beats.scene: The coach rolls between the Spanish lines while enemy soldiers salute
beats.summary: The coach rolls straight through the Spanish lines, and the astonished Spanish soldiers lower their guns and salute it.

beats.scene: Ragueneau drives the coach, and Roxane steps out smiling
beats.summary: Ragueneau, in splendid livery, drives the coach into the camp, and Roxane steps out, smiling, to the astonishment of the soldiers.

beats.scene: Roxane says she crossed the Spanish lines by smiling
beats.summary: Roxane explains that she crossed the Spanish lines by telling every officer that she was going to her love, and they let her through.

beats.scene: Ragueneau opens the coach and reveals hams, pies and wine
beats.summary: Ragueneau opens the boot of the coach and shows hams, pies, chickens and wine, and the starving Cadets cheer.

beats.scene: The Cadets feast politely while Roxane serves them
beats.summary: The Cadets feast, a little shy and very polite, while Roxane serves them with her own hands and thanks each one.

beats.scene: The Comte de Guiche arrives and bows to Roxane
beats.summary: The Comte de Guiche arrives, the Cadets stiffen, and he is surprised to see Roxane, but he bows to her politely.

beats.scene: The Comte warns that a great attack will come at dawn
beats.summary: The Comte warns the Cadets that the Spanish will attack in force at dawn, and he advises Roxane to leave at once.

beats.scene: The Comte decides to stay and fight with the Cadets
beats.summary: The Comte decides to stay with the Cadets and fight, to the surprise of all, and Cyrano grudgingly admires him.

beats.scene: Roxane asks for Christian and Cyrano brings him
beats.summary: Roxane asks where Christian is, and Cyrano goes to fetch him, with a heavy heart.

beats.scene: Roxane and Christian sit alone while the Cadets eat at a distance
beats.summary: While the Cadets eat at a distance, Roxane and Christian sit alone, and she tells him that his letters have made her love him more than ever.

beats.scene: Roxane speaks softly to Christian on a log, with the camp behind them
beats.summary: Roxane tells Christian that at first she loved his face, but now she loves his soul, as it shines in his letters.

beats.scene: Roxane says she would love Christian even if he were ugly
beats.summary: Roxane says that she would love Christian even if he were ugly, because it is his soul that she loves.

beats.scene: Christian understands that she loves Cyrano's words, not his own
beats.summary: Christian goes white as he understands that Roxane is in love with Cyrano's words, and not with him.

beats.scene: Roxane reads from his letters and Christian shivers
beats.summary: Roxane takes a letter from her dress and reads a passage aloud, and each tender word makes Christian suffer.

beats.scene: Roxane goes to rest in the coach while Christian watches her walk away
beats.summary: Roxane goes to rest with the Duenna in the coach, and Christian watches her walk away across the grass.

beats.scene: Christian tells Cyrano that Roxane loves him, not Christian
beats.summary: Christian goes to Cyrano and tells him that it is Cyrano that Roxane truly loves, not Christian.

beats.scene: Christian insists that Cyrano tell Roxane the whole truth
beats.summary: Christian insists that Cyrano tell Roxane the whole truth and let her choose between them, whatever she may decide.

beats.scene: Cyrano refuses at first and then slowly agrees
beats.summary: Cyrano refuses at first, afraid that the truth will lose her for both of them, but then he slowly agrees to tell her.

beats.scene: Christian goes to find Roxane and Cyrano waits alone
beats.summary: Christian walks off to fetch Roxane, and Cyrano waits alone, afraid of what he must say and of what she may answer.

beats.scene: A cannon booms in the distance and the Cadets seize their arms
beats.summary: A cannon booms in the distance and a drum begins to roll, and the Cadets seize their arms, because the great attack has begun.

beats.scene: Spanish soldiers charge across the field in the early light
beats.summary: The Spanish army charges across the field in great numbers, and the Comte de Guiche orders the Cadets to hold the line.

beats.scene: Roxane is hurried to safety in the coach
beats.summary: Roxane is hurried into the coach by Ragueneau and the Duenna, and she is driven away to a safer place.

beats.scene: Christian charges forward to protect a friend and is struck down
beats.summary: Christian charges forward bravely to protect a wounded friend, and a bullet strikes him down.

beats.scene: Cyrano runs to Christian's side and kneels
beats.summary: Cyrano sees Christian fall and runs across the field to kneel at his side, ignoring the bullets that whistle past.

beats.scene: Christian asks whether Cyrano told Roxane, and Cyrano lies
beats.summary: Christian whispers a question: did Cyrano tell her the truth? Cyrano tells a kind lie, that Roxane loves Christian above all.

beats.scene: Christian dies, and Cyrano finds a letter over his heart
beats.summary: Christian smiles and dies in Cyrano's arms, and Cyrano finds a last letter over his heart, written in Christian's name.

beats.scene: Cyrano rises with his sword and leads the Cadets in a charge
beats.summary: Cyrano rises with tears on his face and his sword in his hand and leads the Cadets in a furious charge against the enemy.

beats.scene: The Spanish retreat and the field falls silent
beats.summary: At last the Spanish retreat, many brave Cadets have fallen, and the field falls silent in the smoke.

beats.scene: Roxane kneels beside Christian and takes a stained letter from his coat
beats.summary: Roxane returns to the field, kneels beside Christian, and takes the stained letter from his coat.

beats.scene: Roxane reads the last letter and weeps while Cyrano listens in silence
beats.summary: Roxane reads the last letter and weeps, and Cyrano, who knows every word, hears them again in silence.

beats.scene: Roxane in black walks into a convent gate while Cyrano watches
beats.summary: Roxane retires to a convent to mourn Christian, and Cyrano, saying nothing of the truth, promises to visit her.

beats.scene: Autumn leaves fall in the convent garden under a great tree, fifteen years later
beats.summary: Fifteen years later, in the autumn of 1655, the convent garden is quiet, and golden leaves are falling from a great tree.

beats.scene: Sister Marthe and Sister Claire whisper about Roxane
beats.summary: Sister Marthe and Sister Claire whisper in the garden that Roxane is as faithful in her grief as any saint, and still sad.

beats.scene: Roxane embroiders in black with Christian's last letter on her heart
beats.summary: Roxane, in black, sits at her embroidery by the tree and wears Christian's last letter on a ribbon over her heart.

beats.scene: Every Saturday Cyrano visits Roxane and amuses her with the news of Paris
beats.summary: Every Saturday for fifteen years Cyrano has visited Roxane and amused her with the news of Paris, and he has never once been late.

beats.scene: Cyrano's poor, proud life over fifteen years of freedom
beats.summary: In those fifteen years Cyrano has stayed poor and proud, refused every patron and made a great many new enemies.

beats.scene: Le Bret and Ragueneau worry to Roxane that Cyrano is poor and in danger
beats.summary: Le Bret and Ragueneau tell Roxane in the garden that Cyrano is poor, alone and surrounded by dangerous enemies.

beats.scene: Roxane laughs it off, saying Cyrano is always in danger and always safe
beats.summary: Roxane smiles at their worry and says that Cyrano has been in danger all his life and has always come out of it laughing.

beats.scene: The Duke de Guiche, now a great nobleman, visits Roxane and admires Cyrano
beats.summary: The Duke de Guiche, now a great nobleman, visits Roxane, admits that he envies Cyrano and warns her that the poet's enemies are dangerous.

beats.scene: The Duke leaves and Roxane waits for the last stroke of the hour
beats.summary: The Duke leaves, the bells begin to strike the hour, and Roxane waits for the last stroke, when Cyrano always arrives, but this time he does not.

beats.scene: A heavy log falls from a high window onto a man walking below
beats.summary: As Cyrano walks to the convent, someone drops a heavy log on his head from a window above the street.

beats.scene: Cyrano struggles up and hides the wound under his hat
beats.summary: Cyrano struggles to his feet, pulls his hat low over the wound, and decides that nothing in the world will make him late.

beats.scene: Cyrano climbs the road to the convent, resting against walls
beats.summary: Cyrano climbs slowly toward the convent, leaning on walls and resting on steps, with his sword as a walking stick.

beats.scene: Cyrano arrives pale at the garden gate, and Roxane tells him he is late
beats.summary: Cyrano appears at the garden gate, pale and weak, and Roxane teases him that he is late for the first time in fifteen years.

beats.scene: Cyrano sits down with Roxane and jokes about the week's news
beats.summary: Cyrano sits on the bench beside Roxane, and with all his old wit he begins to tell her the news and gossip of the week.

beats.scene: Roxane notices that Cyrano is pale and that his voice grows faint
beats.summary: Roxane notices that Cyrano is very pale and that his voice grows faint, and he says it is only the old wound from Arras.

beats.scene: Roxane says she has an old wound too, and shows the letter
beats.summary: Roxane says that everyone has an old wound, and she touches the little bag that holds Christian's last letter.

beats.scene: Cyrano asks to read the letter and Roxane gives it to him
beats.summary: Cyrano asks to read the letter that she keeps over her heart, and Roxane, surprised, gives it to him.

beats.scene: Cyrano unfolds the letter and begins to read aloud as the light fades
beats.summary: Cyrano unfolds the old letter and begins to read it aloud, while the sun sinks behind the trees and the light fades.

beats.scene: Cyrano reads the words of the farewell letter as the shadows lengthen
beats.summary: Cyrano reads the words of the farewell letter, in which the writer says goodbye to Roxane and promises to love her beyond death.

beats.scene: Dusk gathers in the garden as Cyrano keeps reading from the paper
beats.summary: Dusk gathers in the garden, and Cyrano goes on reading the letter in a steady voice as the page grows dark.

beats.scene: Roxane notices that it is too dark to read
beats.summary: Roxane suddenly notices that it is far too dark to read, and yet Cyrano's voice has not stopped for a single word.

beats.scene: Roxane stands and remembers the voice under the balcony
beats.summary: Roxane rises from the bench, stares at Cyrano and remembers the voice under the balcony, speaking out of the dark.

beats.scene: Roxane cries that it was Cyrano all along
beats.summary: Roxane cries out that it was he all along, the voice, the letters and the soul that she loved.

beats.scene: Cyrano denies it at first and says it was Christian
beats.summary: Cyrano denies it at first and says that it was Christian whom she loved, but his voice shakes and he cannot hide the truth.

beats.scene: Roxane says she should have known from the tears on the page
beats.summary: Roxane says she should have known when she saw the tears on the letter, because they were Cyrano's own and not Christian's.

beats.scene: Cyrano says Christian was handsome while he was only the voice
beats.summary: Cyrano explains that Christian was handsome and brave, while he himself was only the voice, and he never wanted her pity.

beats.scene: Roxane weeps that she has lost the man she loved twice
beats.summary: Roxane weeps that she has loved one soul all her life, and that she has lost it twice, once to the war and once to the truth.

beats.scene: Le Bret and Ragueneau run into the garden, frightened
beats.summary: Le Bret and Ragueneau run into the garden, out of breath, and cry that Cyrano walked here with a terrible wound.

beats.scene: Roxane sees the blood under Cyrano's hat
beats.summary: Roxane sees the blood under Cyrano's hat and understands that he has been dying all through the afternoon.

beats.scene: Cyrano rises from the bench, refusing every helping hand, and draws his sword
beats.summary: Cyrano refuses all help, rises from the bench and draws his sword, saying that he will not die lying down.

beats.scene: Cyrano fights the shadows and names his enemies
beats.summary: Cyrano fights the shadows in the air and names his enemies: Falsehood, Compromise, Prejudice, and many more.

beats.scene: Cyrano cries that Cowardice and Folly will not defeat him
beats.summary: Cyrano cries that Cowardice and Folly will never defeat him, because he has never once yielded to them in all his life.

beats.scene: Cyrano leans against the tree and says that Time will strike him down
beats.summary: Cyrano leans against the great tree and says that, yes, at last he knows that Time will strike him down, but he fights on all the same.

beats.scene: Roxane begs Cyrano to live because she loves him
beats.summary: Roxane begs Cyrano to live, because she has loved him all along, but he gently says that it is too late.

beats.scene: Cyrano jokes about Molière and Christian
beats.summary: Cyrano jokes with Le Bret that Molière borrowed a scene from his comedy, and that fate has always given others the genius or the good looks.

beats.scene: Cyrano speaks of the moon, where Socrates and Galileo wait
beats.summary: As the moon rises, Cyrano smiles and says that he is going there, where he will find Socrates and Galileo to talk with.

beats.scene: Cyrano says that time will take everything, but not one thing
beats.summary: Cyrano says that Time may take his laurels and his roses, but there is one thing it can never take from him.

beats.scene: Cyrano names his panache and Roxane kisses his forehead
beats.summary: Cyrano says that the one thing he will take with him is his panache, and Roxane bends and kisses his forehead.

beats.scene: Cyrano dies in the garden, and Roxane stays beside him as the leaves fall
beats.summary: Cyrano dies in the garden, and Roxane is left weeping, with his panache remembered as his true gift.

A1A2: In Paris, a crowd waits for a play in a big old theatre.
Thieves move through the crowd, and the men hold their money tight.
Christian, a handsome young soldier, waits to see the lady he loves.
Ligniere, a poet who loves wine, tells Christian the lady's name.
A rich lord wants Roxane too, and he has great power.
Christian is sad, because he cannot find the words for a lady.
The crowd talks about a man called Cyrano and his big nose.
Roxane comes into her box, and Christian cannot say a word.
At last the play begins, and the fat actor walks onto the stage.
A loud voice cries out, and the actor stops speaking at once.
Cyrano stands on a chair, and his nose is very big.
Cyrano says he will count to three, and then the actor must go.
Some people shout for Cyrano, and some shout for the play.
Cyrano asks who wants to fight, but no one comes forward.
Cyrano gives the manager a purse of gold for the lost play.
A man asks why Cyrano hates the actor, but Cyrano will not say.
A young lord laughs at Cyrano's nose, and Cyrano is not pleased.
Cyrano says the lord could have made much better jokes.
Cyrano makes more jokes about his nose, and the crowd laughs.
Cyrano says the lord has no wit, so they will fight.
The crowd moves back, and Cyrano takes off his heavy cloak.
The swords touch, and Cyrano begins to speak his poem.
The lord attacks again and again, but he cannot hit Cyrano.
Roxane leans forward in her box, and her eyes are bright.
Cyrano tells the lord when the sword will touch him.
At the last line, Cyrano hits him, and the lord falls down.
The crowd shouts Cyrano's name, and the angry Comte leaves.
Le Bret says Cyrano is a fool, but a very brave fool.
Cyrano says he wants to be free, even if he is poor.
At last Cyrano says he loves his cousin Roxane.
Cyrano says no woman could love a man with his nose.
Le Bret says Roxane liked the fight, but Cyrano is not sure.
Roxane's old servant comes in and asks for Cyrano.
Roxane wants to see Cyrano tomorrow, and he is surprised.
Cyrano is so happy that he feels he could fight an army.
Ligniere runs in, afraid, and says a hundred men wait for him.
Cyrano says he will take Ligniere home and meet the men.
Cyrano asks people to bring lights and watch the fight.
A long line of lights walks through the dark streets of Paris.
Cyrano fights a hundred men alone, and he wins the fight.
At dawn, the ovens are hot in the pastry shop.
Workers wrap the cakes in pages covered with poems.
Ragueneau sings a cake recipe, and the workers listen.
Cyrano comes in tired but happy, and Ragueneau is amazed.
Cyrano asks for a quiet shop when the lady comes.
Cyrano writes a letter of love and wonders if he can give it.
The old servant comes, and Cyrano gives her many sweet cakes.
Roxane comes in with a smile and takes Cyrano's hands.
Roxane remembers when they played together as children in the country.
Roxane thanks Cyrano for beating the man the Comte likes.
Roxane says she has a secret and needs her cousin's help.
Roxane says she loves a man, and Cyrano turns pale.
Roxane loves a young man in Cyrano's company of soldiers.
Cyrano asks if the man is clever, and he tries to smile.
Roxane is afraid the other soldiers will fight with him.
Cyrano promises to help, and Roxane is very happy.
Roxane thanks Cyrano and leaves with the old servant.
Alone, Cyrano laughs sadly, because he must help his rival.
Soldiers from Gascony rush in, loud and happy, to cheer Cyrano.
The soldiers are hungry and poor, but they are very proud.
The soldiers beg for the story, but Cyrano says little.
The Comte de Guiche comes in, and the soldiers are quiet.
The Comte says the Cardinal could help Cyrano's play.
The Comte says the Cardinal would change just a few lines.
Cyrano says no, because he will not change one word of his play.
Le Bret is sad, but the soldiers cheer Cyrano's answer.
The Comte leaves angrily, and Cyrano makes a joke about it.
A new soldier called Christian comes into the shop.
Christian makes a joke about Cyrano's nose, and everyone is silent.
Cyrano turns white, but he does not touch his sword.
Cyrano takes Christian aside and says he is Roxane's cousin.
Cyrano says Roxane loves Christian, and Christian is very happy.
Christian says he cannot speak well, and he is afraid.
Cyrano has an idea: he will give Christian the words.
Christian says yes, and Cyrano gives him a letter.
Every night, Cyrano sits and writes a new letter by candle.
Roxane reads each letter and loves Christian more each day.
A tear falls on the page, and Cyrano is very sad.
Ragueneau is ruined, and his wife has left him.
Cyrano finds Ragueneau a new job in Roxane's house.
Weeks later, evening comes to Roxane's quiet house with the balcony.
Ragueneau works in the kitchen and writes poems about the bread.
Roxane says Christian is coming tonight, and she is excited.
Roxane reads a letter aloud, and the servant is not sure.
A servant says the Comte de Guiche is at the door.
The Comte says he leaves for the war tonight.
The Comte says the Cadets of Gascony will go to war too.
Roxane has an idea: keep the Cadets in Paris, away from the war.
The Comte likes the idea and says he will give the order.
The Comte leaves, and Roxane hurries to wait for Christian.
Christian says he will speak for himself tonight.
Roxane comes to the balcony, but Christian says only that he loves her.
Roxane is sad and goes back into the house.
Christian calls for Cyrano, who comes out of the dark.
Cyrano hides under the balcony, and Roxane comes out again.
Cyrano whispers words, and Christian says them slowly.
Cyrano pushes Christian away and speaks for himself in the dark.
Cyrano speaks of the stars, and Roxane's heart flies.
Roxane asks for a kiss, and Cyrano says what a kiss is.
Christian climbs up to Roxane, and Cyrano watches in the dark.
The old servant says a monk is at the door for Roxane.
The old monk gives Roxane a letter from the Comte.
Roxane reads the letter aloud, but she changes the words.
The honest old monk believes her and agrees to help.
Roxane takes the monk and Christian inside the house.
Alone in the street, Cyrano thinks about the wedding.
A man in a mask comes along the street, and Cyrano knows him.
Cyrano drops from above and lands in front of the Comte.
Cyrano says he has just fallen from the moon.
Cyrano tells a long, silly story, and the Comte listens.
The monk comes out of the house, and Cyrano stops talking.
Roxane and Christian are happy and tell the Comte they are married.
The Comte sees that they tricked him, and he is very angry.
The Comte shouts that the Cadets must go to war at once.
Roxane begs the Comte, but he says no and walks away.
Roxane asks Cyrano to keep Christian safe and make him write.
Roxane says a sad goodbye to Christian in the dark.
Drums beat in the street, and the soldiers form a line.
The soldiers march away, and Roxane waves from her balcony.
On the road, Cyrano writes the first war letter by a fire.
At Arras, grey dawn comes over a cold, muddy camp.
The Cadets have not eaten for days, and they are thin.
An old soldier plays a tune from home, and some men weep.
Cyrano arrives and makes the sad soldiers laugh.
Before dawn, Cyrano slips out of the camp with a letter.
Cyrano crawls past the Spanish soldiers in the mist.
Cyrano comes back with a hole in his hat, and Le Bret is angry.
Christian asks why Cyrano goes out each day, and Cyrano answers.
Christian asks what Cyrano wrote, and Cyrano says some lines.
A soldier shouts that a coach is coming across the fields.
The coach rolls through the Spanish soldiers, and they salute it.
Ragueneau stops the coach, and Roxane steps out, smiling.
Roxane tells the men how she came through the enemy.
Ragueneau opens the coach, and it is full of food.
The Cadets eat, and Roxane serves them with a smile.
The Comte de Guiche comes and sees Roxane, and bows.
The Comte says the Spanish will attack at dawn.
The Comte decides to stay and fight, and the Cadets are surprised.
Roxane asks where Christian is, and Cyrano goes to find him.
Roxane and Christian sit alone, and she says she loves his letters.
Roxane says she once loved his face, but now she loves his soul.
Roxane says she would love him even if he were not handsome.
Christian understands that Roxane loves Cyrano's words, not his own.
Roxane reads a letter aloud, and each word hurts Christian.
Roxane goes to rest, and Christian watches her walk away.
Christian tells Cyrano that Roxane truly loves him.
Christian wants Cyrano to tell Roxane the truth.
Cyrano says no at first, but then he agrees.
Christian goes to find Roxane, and Cyrano waits alone.
A cannon booms, and the Cadets grab their swords and guns.
The Spanish army charges, and the Cadets stand in a line.
Roxane is taken away in the coach to a safer place.
Christian runs to help a friend and is shot.
Cyrano sees Christian fall, and runs to kneel beside him.
Christian asks if Cyrano told her, and Cyrano tells a kind lie.
Christian smiles, and he dies in Cyrano's arms.
Cyrano jumps up with his sword and leads the soldiers forward.
The enemy runs away, and the field is silent at last.
Roxane runs to Christian and finds the letter in his coat.
Roxane reads the last letter and cries, and Cyrano is silent.
Roxane goes to live in a convent, and Cyrano promises to visit.
Fifteen years later, it is autumn in the quiet convent garden.
Two nuns talk softly about Roxane and her long sadness.
Roxane sews in the garden and wears Christian's letter.
Every Saturday, Cyrano visits Roxane, and he is never late.
Cyrano has stayed poor and proud, and he has many enemies.
Le Bret and Ragueneau say that Cyrano is poor and in danger.
Roxane smiles and says Cyrano is always in danger and safe.
The Duke de Guiche visits Roxane and says he admires Cyrano.
The bells strike the hour, but Cyrano does not come.
Someone drops a heavy log on Cyrano's head from a window.
Cyrano stands up slowly, and he pulls his hat down low.
Cyrano walks slowly to the convent and rests on the walls.
Cyrano comes at last, pale, and Roxane says he is late.
Cyrano sits beside Roxane and tells the news of the week.
Roxane sees that Cyrano is pale, and he says it is nothing.
Roxane says she has an old wound too, and she shows the bag.
Cyrano asks to read the letter, and Roxane gives it to him.
Cyrano opens the old letter and begins to read it aloud.
Cyrano reads the letter: it says goodbye and promises love.
Night is coming, but Cyrano keeps on reading the letter.
Roxane sees that it is too dark to read, but he goes on.
Roxane stands and remembers the voice in the dark long ago.
Roxane cries out that it was Cyrano all the time.
Cyrano says it was not him, but his voice shakes.
Roxane says she should have known from the tears on the page.
Cyrano says Christian was handsome, and he was only a voice.
Roxane holds his hand and cries, because she has lost him twice.
Le Bret and Ragueneau run in and cry that Cyrano is hurt.
Roxane sees the blood under Cyrano's hat, and she is afraid.
Cyrano stands up and takes out his sword to fight.
Cyrano fights the air and shouts the names of his enemies.
Cyrano says Cowardice and Folly will never win.
Cyrano leans on the tree and says he will fight until the end.
Roxane begs Cyrano to live, and he says it is too late.
Cyrano jokes that Molière borrowed a scene from him.
As the moon rises, Cyrano says that he is going there.
Cyrano says Time can take much, but not one thing.
Cyrano says he will take his panache, and Roxane kisses him.
Cyrano dies in the garden, and Roxane stays beside him.
B1B2: In the year 1640, a noisy crowd fills a theatre in Paris called the Hôtel de Bourgogne. Nobles, soldiers, thieves and poets all push and talk, waiting for the play to begin.
Pickpockets slip between the gentlemen, and every man keeps one hand on his purse. The pages dash about playing tricks, and nobody minds, because the play is very late.
Christian de Neuvillette is a handsome young man who has just joined an army company. He is in love with a lady in the theatre, but he has never spoken to her.
Christian asks a poet named Ligniere, who knows everyone in Paris. Ligniere smiles, lifts his cup and tells him that the lady's name is Roxane.
Ligniere warns Christian that the powerful Comte de Guiche wants Roxane as well. The Comte plans to marry her to a weak young nobleman who will always do as he is told.
Christian sadly shakes his head and says he is no poet. When he tries to speak to a clever woman, his tongue turns to stone and every fine word runs away.

All around them the crowd is talking about a Gascon swordsman and poet called Cyrano, who is famous for his enormous nose. Cyrano has ordered the fat actor Montfleury not to appear on any stage for a month.
A hush runs through the front benches as Roxane takes her seat in the box, followed by her old servant. Christian stares up at her, and for a moment he forgets how to breathe.

The Comte de Guiche and the Vicomte de Valvert take their chairs at the side of the stage, and the crowd falls silent. At last the play begins, and the fat actor Montfleury walks out to speak his first lines.
Montfleury has hardly spoken ten lines when a voice like thunder rings out from the middle of the crowd. It asks the actor, very angrily, whether he has forgotten the order he was given.
Cyrano stands on a chair in the middle of the crowd, with his arms folded and his hat tilted over one eye. His nose is so large that for a moment the people near him can look at nothing else.
Cyrano tells Montfleury that he will count to three. At the third count, he says, the actor's round moon of a face must disappear from the stage.
The crowd splits into two noisy camps, with some cheering Cyrano and others shouting for the play to go on. Poor Montfleury stands frozen on the stage and cannot decide what to do.
Cyrano shouts that he will cut off the ears of any man who dislikes his order. He turns slowly around, but not one person is brave enough to step out.
Bellerose, the manager, complains that his evening is ruined and the people want their money back. Cyrano laughs and throws him a heavy purse of gold, and the crowd cheers his generosity.
A curious marquis asks why Cyrano hates Montfleury so much. Cyrano gives two reasons: the first is that the man acts very badly, and the second he keeps to himself.
The Vicomte de Valvert steps forward, hoping to please the Comte, and says in a bored voice that Cyrano has a very large nose. Cyrano bows politely and agrees that it is indeed very large.
Cyrano asks whether that is really all the Vicomte can say, since a clever man could say so much more. He begins with a fierce one: if he had such a nose, he would cut it off at once.
Cyrano goes on with a gentle joke, a curious joke and a polite joke, each one funnier than the last. The crowd laughs louder every time, and the Vicomte turns red.

Cyrano says that the Vicomte has neither wit nor manners, and that he only dared to laugh because he was sure no one would answer. Then he offers a duel in which he will make up a poem at the same time.
The crowd pushes back to make a ring, and Cyrano throws off his cloak and his hat. He names his ballad after the duel at the Hôtel de Bourgogne and takes his place.
As soon as the swords touch, Cyrano begins his poem in a cheerful, steady voice. He says each line in time with his blade, as calmly as if he were taking a walk.
The Vicomte attacks again and again, but his sword only meets empty air. Cyrano turns every thrust aside and never loses a single rhyme.
In her box, Roxane leans forward with shining eyes, and Christian is watching her as closely as she is watching the duel. Across the stage, the Comte de Guiche is frowning.
Cyrano warns the sweating Vicomte that the poem is nearly finished. At the very last line, he says, the point of his sword will touch him.
At the very last line of the poem, Cyrano lunges, just as he promised. The Vicomte staggers and falls, hurt but alive, and the whole theatre erupts in cheers.
The crowd shouts Cyrano's name, and he bows to the left and to the right. The Comte de Guiche walks out in anger, while the Vicomte is carried away by his friends.
When the theatre is nearly empty, Cyrano's friend Le Bret comes to him. He praises the fight, but he scolds Cyrano for making so many powerful enemies in a single night.
Cyrano answers that he would rather be free than rich. He does not want a patron, a pension or a protector, and he will gladly fight enemies alone.
Le Bret asks about the second reason for the quarrel with Montfleury. Cyrano lowers his voice and admits that he loves his cousin Roxane, and that the fat actor had dared to stare at her.
Le Bret asks why Cyrano does not simply tell her. Cyrano touches his great nose and says that no woman, least of all a beautiful one, could ever love a face like his.
Le Bret reminds him that Roxane watched the duel with shining eyes and seemed delighted. Cyrano shrugs and says that a woman will always smile at a man who is brave, so it means nothing.
As the two friends talk, a knock sounds at the door. It is Roxane's old servant, the Duenna, who asks politely whether she may speak to Monsieur de Bergerac.

Le Bret and Ragueneau run into the garden, out of breath and frightened. They cry out that Cyrano is hurt, because someone dropped a log on his head, and he walked all the way here.
Roxane lifts his hat and sees the blood, and she understands everything at once. Cyrano has been dying all through the afternoon, and he has been telling her the news with a smile.

Cyrano fights the shadows in the air and cries out the names of his old enemies. Falsehood, Compromise and Prejudice are all there, and he strikes at each of them in turn.

Christian listened with a sinking heart, for he had neither rank nor fortune with which to answer such a rival.

Christian looked down at his plain soldier's coat and shook his head with a bitter little laugh. In the company of ladies, he said, he was as dumb as a stone, and he had no notion how to change it.
